The test image shows a sugarcane plant at soil level with:
- Straw/tan dried-out leaves, wilted and dying
- Reddish-brown discoloration at the base/crown
- Whole plant appears to be dying from the base upward
- No visible leaf spots, mosaic, or streak patterns

This looks like a base/crown rot — candidates: **Sett_Rot** (base rotting from seed piece) or **Pokkah_Boeng** (growing point rot). Let me view one reference from each top candidate, then two more classes.
Sett_Rot reference shows very similar pattern: straw-colored dying leaves with dark rotted base. Strong visual match. Now checking Pokkah_Boeng.
Pokkah_Boeng reference shows a stem with pinkish discoloration — doesn't match the whole-plant wilting pattern in the test image. Now checking two more classes to fulfill the 4-class requirement.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Small sugarcane plant at soil level, completely dried out with straw/tan wilted leaves, dark reddish-brown rot at the crown/base. Plant is essentially dead.
- **Sett_Rot** (LeafNet_136): Near-identical — dying plant with straw-colored leaves and dark rotted base at soil level. Strong match.
- **Pokkah_Boeng** (LeafNet_100): Shows stem with pinkish discoloration only. No match.
- **Yellow_Leaf** (LeafNet_47): Plant still mostly green with some browning. No match.
- **Grassy_Shoot** (LeafNet_14): Shows proliferation of thin shoots. No match.

The test image is a textbook Sett_Rot presentation: the seed piece has rotted at the base, causing the whole young plant to die and desiccate.
